story_text:
At again, we believe the future of energy shouldn’t come at the expense of what we’ve already built. Millions of rechargeable battery cells are thrown away before they reach the end of their usable lives. That’s why we designed our again, 6,000 mAh and 10,000 mAh portable power banks, using cells recovered from decommissioned electric vehicles and electronics.
By testing, sorting cells, and validating each pack as a complete system, we’re able to deliver consistent performance without compromise, proving that second-life energy can meet modern expectations for quality, safety, and usability.
Video of more detailed demo: https://youtube.com/shorts/PoCk3J29WpU
Is it safe to use repurposed cells?
Yes. Process matters. That's why our entire intake, testing, and packaging process follows UL 1974 guidelines for repurposing lithium-ion batteries. Every single cell is tested. Every single time. Cells that do not pass their tests are promptly recycled. Cells that pass, find their way into our new chargers, designed to UL 2056 guidelines.
At the again battery website you can type in the serial number of your charger to immediately learn about the cells in your charger. You'll see their capacity and internal resistance testing results as well as how they spent their first life.
Where do we source our batteries?
- The journey of again began in 2020. My electric skateboard broke, but I didn't want to throw it away. The first again cells were sourced in-house.
- In 2021, I began pursuing my electrical engineering degree at The Ohio State University. As the idea behind again gained traction on Etsy, I started sourcing cells from an electronics recycling facility in Columbus. These cells were reclaimed from damaged electric rental scooters and e-bikes.
- Today, we still source from the recycling facility in Columbus. We've also added a few battery collection centers to our network to increase outreach and build a reliable supplier network.
How much life is left in these cells?
- We've been repurposing cells on Etsy, making chargers out of Altoids tins for the past 5 years. We repurposed over 6000 cells. This experience has demonstrated to us that over 95% of recovered cells are testing within 90% of their original capacity. Indicating at least another 5 years of frequent use.
Comment down below, or email us at support@againbattery.com if you have any questions!
risks: Two main things need to occur before we can deliver orders: 1. Verify compliance to FCC Part 15b. 2. Complete UN 38.3 testing so the batteries can be safely shipped worldwide. Because our chargers utilize switching regulators operating over 9kHz to charge and discharge the batteries, we need to verify that our circuit board layout does not interfere with other electronic devices. Following success of this test we will write an SDoC. Both of these milestones take time to meet. We are confident in our ability to meet these milestones thanks to our multiple years of experience shipping portable chargers through Etsy. We have already sold over 2000 portable chargers that use second life batteries through Etsy. Again is being created in an effort to rebrand and legitimize an already de-risked idea. Reach out to us at support@againbattery.com if you have any questions!
